test_summary:
Task 3 Sol repair 4 completed in /home/ingmar/worktrees/ptest/cx-ng-product/task-3 from audited commit c4c3204. Edited only src/ptest/history.py, tests/ng/test_history.py, and this report; preserved the pre-existing untracked Task 3 reports. No commit, merge, push, deployment, global ptest alteration, controller-chain edit, raw test runner, or full-suite run was performed.

Repairs: publication now uses three bounded private records under the writer lock: a generic publication-uncertainty marker, a live publisher identity marker, and a preallocated capacity reserve. Read helpers remain read-only and never create, mutate, or lock history state. They validate the active publisher by PID plus psutil birth time, ignore publication-owned reservation records only while that exact process is alive, and re-read a disappearing publication marker so healthy cleanup cannot create a false disable. A lost or interrupted publisher exposes selection-disabled rather than capacity-exceeded. Actual SQLITE_FULL/quota failure removes the generic marker and atomically promotes the already-created reserve to history-capacity.json without requiring another allocation. Marker payloads are exact allowlists and contain no checkout path, argv, environment, test identifier, or output.

The database is now opened and all publication/reservation/capacity transitions are completed inside the same bounded advisory writer lock. The post-lock _remember_capacity path was removed, so an older failed attempt cannot reacquire the lock and resurrect state after a newer clean full recovery. Capacity errors raised while opening the store occur after reservation and are finalized under that lock. An existing capacity marker is left untouched by committed scoped, skipped, dirty, or older outcomes, preserving the original failed sequence; only a newer validated clean full result with every inventory outcome passed clears it. The strict skipped/xfail rule is unchanged. Generic uncertainty from a lost non-capacity publication intentionally remains fail-closed and requires a later owner-directed CLI recovery design; this task adds no recovery command or public surface. Existing 2 MiB/25 percent compaction behavior is unchanged.

Security-negative contracts: a healthy active writer cannot falsely disable a concurrent read, including the cleanup boundary; an interrupted or dead writer cannot manufacture a safe baseline or a capacity claim; only observed SQLITE_FULL/quota state can expose capacity-exceeded; old failure paths cannot write after releasing the writer lock; concurrent first initialization is serialized and every peer observes a complete schema; reads do not mutate marker, database, or lock state. Identity/authentication are N/A because no credentials or remote identities exist. Authorization/tenancy continue through validated private DomainPaths and checkout identity. Input coverage includes malformed exact marker schemas and injected KeyboardInterrupt/TypeError/FULL failures. State coverage includes publication, cleanup, capacity recovery, and stale-writer interleavings. Exposure is bounded to non-sensitive allowlisted marker fields. Availability remains bounded by the existing two-second writer deadline and finite SQLite recovery candidates. Dependencies remain local filesystem, SQLite, stdlib, and the already-pinned psutil runtime dependency; no network/cloud/model/dependency change was introduced.

Observed RED evidence: scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k 'read_during_healthy or interrupted_publish_is_uncertain or ineligible_commits_preserve or old_capacity_failure_cannot_resurrect' --durations=10 -> 4 failed, 1 passed, 72 deselected in 0.37s. Failures showed healthy in-flight reads reporting capacity-exceeded, KeyboardInterrupt and TypeError leaving a false capacity reason, and an ineligible scoped commit raising the failed sequence from 10 to 20. The first resurrection interleaving initially paused on the later reacquisition and therefore passed; after correcting the test to pause immediately after the original writer-lock release, scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k old_capacity_failure_cannot_resurrect --durations=5 -> 1 failed, 76 deselected in 0.22s, proving the old path entered the writer lock twice. No RED is claimed for the audit-added cleanup-boundary regression.

GREEN evidence: the focused four-contract command above -> 5 passed, 72 deselected in 0.17s. scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k 'capacity or sqlite_full or transient_publish or interrupted_capacity or late_peer or compaction' --durations=10 -> 16 passed, 61 deselected in 0.55s. The first complete owned-module run found one pre-existing concurrency test coupled to peer SQLite BEGIN timing after store opening moved under the writer lock: 76 passed, 1 failed in 7.16s. The test was updated to prove the peer blocks at the writer lock and then observes only the complete schema. The audit-added cleanup-boundary slice scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k 'read_during_healthy_publish' --durations=5 -> 2 passed, 76 deselected in 0.23s. Final required command scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py --durations=10 -> exit 0, 78 passed in 2.09s. Slowest: realistic steady-state inventory 0.38s; both byte-pruning cases 0.17s; substantial freelist compaction 0.14s; all normal tests remained below 0.5s. All test commands used the frozen bootstrap dispatcher with local backend and one worker.

Other required evidence: graphify update . -> exit 0, code-only local AST refresh with 3119 nodes, 5710 edges, and 220 communities; no semantic extraction or source upload. git diff --check -> exit 0 after the source/test changes, and is repeated after this report. Scoped audit-spec review checked the repair brief, frozen design/plan, prior repair evidence, marker state machine and ordering, SQLite transaction/lock boundaries, race sensitivity, privacy, dependency scope, resource cleanup, and test behavior. It found and repaired one cleanup-order false-disable window; the follow-up review has no remaining required finding. Independent approval is not claimed.
concerns: The deliberately persistent selection-disabled marker for an interrupted non-capacity publication has no automatic recovery in Task 3. Per the frozen strict skipped/xfail rule and repair brief, owner-directed recovery belongs to a later owning CLI task.
No full suite was run because the repair brief explicitly prohibits it. Integrated cross-task verification and independent Opus/Astra review remain orchestrator-owned.

Actual SIGKILL/power-loss, PID-reuse stress, kernel ENOSPC, hot-journal recovery, and macOS process-birth behavior were not fault-injected. PID plus psutil birth time guards ordinary process loss and PID reuse; deterministic KeyboardInterrupt, TypeError, SQLITE_FULL, transient SQLite, and thread interleavings are covered.

Bandit, Gitleaks, dependency audit, and property/fuzz gates are not configured in this checkout and were not added out of scope. No dependency, CI, public API, migration, cloud, remote, or model path changed.
Graphify completed with the existing zero-node warnings for review.json and protocol-v1.json; both changed Python files were included in the refreshed local graph.
